Status: exact $M_c$ extrapolated (threshold-law fits for v = 1-4, L = 1, 2; geometric basis extrapolation of the crossing masses for L = 1 v = 1, L = 3, L = 4; lower side not rigorous); upper bound numerically certified at that mass (variational root below threshold, 1e-11 Eh margin for L = 0 and for L = 1 v = 1, L = 3, L = 4); BO and BO+ad from the exact BO / BO+adiabatic zero-energy problems (converged to ≤ 1e-7); offset = M_c(BO+ad) − M_c(exact); predicted offset: parameter-free (non-perturbative fold of the computed non-adiabatic masses m_v(R), m_r(R); no fitted parameter). Columns: upper bound = numerically certified upper bound to M_c (variational root below threshold at that mass; floating point, not interval arithmetic); Delta_na = non-adiabatic offset M_c(BO+ad) − M_c(exact).
$^a$ Pre-specified: prediction frozen 2026-11-14 17:22 before any exact v = 4 calculation; predicted M_c = 98.2627 ± 0.0095, exact 98.26550 ± 0.00011.
$^b$ Pre-specified (second blind test): prediction frozen 2026-11-15 20:17 (sha256-recorded) before any exact crossing was computed; predicted M_c = 17.1072 ± 0.0295, exact 17.094282 (difference -0.0129). Caveat: a scale optimisation of the J = 1, v = 1 basis (N = 12) ran 4 min before the freeze; it computed no crossing (its only information, binding at M = 17.52, was already implied by M_c < M_c(BO+ad)). Frolov & Wardlaw (arXiv:1008.3010) give a basis-limited upper estimate M_c ≈ 17.09444 for this level, consistent with our bound.
$^c$ Secondary pre-specified predictions in the same frozen file: L = 3: 21.3818 ± 0.0295 (exact 21.376199, difference -0.0056); L = 4: 33.9175 ± 0.0295 (exact 33.914349, difference -0.0032).
$^d$ Exploratory: lowest exchange-symmetric J = 1 level (2pσu-like, bound by the long-range polarization well). M_c from a geometric basis extrapolation that is not converged to the level of the other rows (spread of the bases ≈ 0.1); upper bound = rounding-safe crossing of the compact N = 10 + 5 diffuse basis (a larger basis crosses at 813.6015 without margin); BO = 2pσu BO critical mass; no BO+ad (adiabatic correction not available for 2pσu), hence no offset.
Earlier estimates (finite exponential bases, no error bars; first location of these thresholds): lowest L = 1 4.219 (1989), 4.2133 (1994); lowest L = 2 11.485 (1989), bracket 11.489-11.490 (1994); v = 1 10.045, v = 2 30.70, v = 3 61.135, (1,1) 17.125 (1992); (1,1) 17.0944 (2011); Frolov and co-workers, see the main text. All are consistent with the values above. v = 4, L = 3 and L = 4 had not been computed.
Sources: paper1/critical_masses/, paper1/critical_masses_v4/, paper1/rotational/, paper1/bo_offset/massfunc/fold_results.csv, paper1/critical_masses_v4/prediction.json; summary §1, §6, §15; paper1/thresholds_Lv/RESULT.md, *_crossings.csv, prediction_J1v1.json, bo_brackets.txt.

| ddμ | 17.7517 | (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (2,0) | (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (2,0) | (0,2), (2,1), (3,0), (4,0) | 8/8 | (1,1): 3.8% |
| ttμ | 26.5849 | (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (2,0), (3,0) | (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (2,0), (3,0) | (0,2), (2,1), (4,0) | 8/8 | (2,1): 4.0% |

Predictions use our thresholds (Tables T1, T4): (0,1) M > 9.525634; (0,2) M > 29.63939; (1,0) M > 4.2082827; (1,1) M > 17.094282; (2,0) M > 11.4894217; (2,1) M > 27.69724706; (3,0) M > 21.376199; (4,0) M > 33.914349; (0,0) is bound at every M. Odd J are the exchange-antisymmetric levels (L 'A'), even J the symmetric ones (L 'S'). Every level in the three ions, and the absent (0,2) and (4,0), is now compared with a computed threshold: 24/24 statements agree. Closest threshold: smallest relative distance |M/M_c − 1|; all distances exceed the uncertainty of M_c (≤ 1e-5 relative) by orders of magnitude.
Status: level existence only (no energies compared). Presence of a level rests on the numerically certified upper bound (a bound state exists at that mass) together with the observed monotone growth of the binding energy with M; absence rests on the extrapolated M_c (lower side not rigorous). Smallest margins: present (1,1) in ddμ (3.8% above M_c), absent (2,1) in ttμ (4.0% below M_c).
Literature: Frolov & Wardlaw, EPJD 63, 339 (2011), arXiv:1008.3010 (via docs/literature/referee_check_2026-11-15.md, Part B); the same level counts (2, 5, 6 bound states) are restated in Frolov, arXiv:2503.17389 (2025) (docs/literature/frolov_2025_2026_notes.md). M = m_nucleus/m_μ with their masses.

$^a$ Blind test of the threshold map: all predictions frozen 2026-11-16 09:35 (PREDICTION_MAP.md, sha256-recorded) before any exact calculation of these levels. Prediction = parameter-free non-perturbative fold of m_v(R), m_r(R) into the BO+ad zero-energy problem (same code as the earlier blind tests); band ±0.0295 = largest |exact − pred.| of the nine levels known before the freeze (Table T1; level (1,0)); criterion |exact − pred.| ≤ band + exact error. Result: 14/14 PASS, largest |exact − pred.| = 0.0095.
Status: exact M_c = geometric extrapolation in the compact basis size of the crossing masses (lower side not rigorous); certified upper bound = numerically certified upper bound (crossing of E = E_th − 1e-11 Eh, tol 1e-12, tol 1e-14 for (7,0); variational root below threshold at that mass; floating point, not interval arithmetic); BO and BO+ad from the exact BO / BO+adiabatic zero-energy problems (bo_map.json).
$^b$ L = 6: the compact-size sequence is not monotone and the extrapolation is unreliable (for (6,1) it lies above the best crossing). Value = best crossing (rigorous upper bound up to rounding, margin 0), with a one-sided error = max(|best − extrapolated| + extrapolation error, largest compact-size step); the difference and PASS use this value (with the extrapolated value: −0.0013 and −0.0025, also PASS).
$^c$ The extrapolated (4,1) value 57.16494981(46) lies 7.4e-7 above the best crossing 57.164949070 (and above the certified bound): the extrapolation error is underestimated by about a factor 2; irrelevant at the 0.03 level.
$^d$ (7,0): the double-precision L = 7 basis failed validation (canonical-orthogonalization truncation at tol 1e-12, precision loss at 1e-14; threshold_map/validate_L7_diagnostics.md). Computed instead with double-double (about 32-digit) assembly of the overlap and Hamiltonian matrices, single-pass canonical orthogonalization at tol 1e-14 and spurious-root guards (paper1/threshold_map_L7hp; validate_L 7 passes; L = 6 control reproduces double precision to 2e-10). Value = best crossing 87.5214689 (N = 12 + 2 diffuse) minus the geometric compact-size correction; certified bound at tol 1e-14 (not 1e-12).
Sources: paper1/threshold_map/RESULT.md (2026-11-17), data/*_crossings.csv, threshold_map_L7hp/data/J7v0_crossings.csv, prediction_map.json, bo_map.json.

Unequal masses {A+, B+, e−}, m_B = q m_A; M_c = mass of the light nucleus A (in m_e). Theory = two-channel (g/u) model with the non-adiabatic mass functions (2ch+m), predictions frozen 2026-11-16 09:48 (sha256-recorded) before the first exact run. Band (frozen): model-variant spread + the symmetric-family residual of the same level scaled by (1+q)/(2q), floor 0.03 (0.0368 for (1,0)); lenient criterion 0.10 (also frozen).
Result: 0/7 within the frozen band, 3/7 within 0.10. Every theory residual is negative (the theory overestimates M_c by 0.04-0.18). Null models: NS = BO+ad minus the exact symmetric-family offset of the same level; NT = the same from the exact threshold; NP = persistence (offset of the previous J = 0 level; (0,2)-(0,4) only). The smallest null-model miss is 4-43 times the theory miss.
Status: exact M_c = extrapolated (geometric in compact size); certified upper bound as in Table T4 (margin 1e-11 Eh). Validation at q = 1 (unsymmetrized code): the production basis gives 9.587305 vs the symmetric exact 9.525634; with the mirror basis (diffuse ladder also in the closed channel) 9.52565573 (9.52564891 with a larger basis), i.e. +1.5e-5 from the exact value. The same enlargements shift the q = 2 and q = 1.5 (0,1) values by ≤ 1.2e-6 (L = 0 only; (1,0), (2,0) not covered).
Sources: paper1/unequal_masses/RESULT.md (2026-11-16 17:28), prediction_unequal.json, *_crossings.csv.
